build.execution_boundary: Original full.validate_build internally executes the preserved ELF --hash-file as a hash utility. It does not compile or run a measurement. Call only once for a newly received build and retain complete original return/stdio/exit.
build.reuse: Retain original returned outer/built/binary and exact sealed files inventory for subsequent same-study shard validation; no repeated validate_build.

matrix.intake_boundary: Retain original aggregate receipt and its actual producer execution evidence. Any local invocation, if needed after original artifacts exist, must be separately requested and recorded; do not pre-execute aggregate or manufacture passed.
matrix.original_predicate: combine requires every expected unique slot and one source/binary/driver/build/run/attempt identity, complete original closure and parity; 45 cells and 85 records.

shard.execution_boundary: One original function call for each newly received complete slot; original inner validator can invoke ELF --hash-file for plan/raw digests. No product measurement or rebuilding.
shard.result: Retain the entire original returned object, including all 2 records per mutation cell or 1 fanout record; do not substitute progress prefixes.

scope_limits: This is an independent N1 descriptive task population, not the old 150-cell or 1350-cell study.
Five no_op setup records are the preselected cold curve subset of forty setup records; retain the other 35.
Native five-hour deadline, seed, all rows/15-table parity and resource budgets are unchanged.
No stable-tail statistics or automatic task status updates.
Current product authorship and host execution receipt are separate from pr_triage independent semantic review.
transport_scope: Root uniquely downloads/materializes new official artifacts; reuse already recorded CRC rather than double traversal.
For a new ZIP retain whole bytes, official ID/name/size/digest/source/run/attempt, safe member paths/modes and CRC/hash record.
Original failed data and partial uploads remain original failures/unknowns. Native result and byte custody are distinct.
Progress records/ACKs retain exact offset/hash coverage and unknown tail; they do not replace full shard artifacts or increase accepted records.
